key_insight: A 3D CNN using velocity, density, and log-transformed targets can better learn subgrid Reynolds stress transport in quiet-Sun radiative hydrodynamic simulations than MLP and classical turbulence closures.
engineering_relevance: This provides a data-driven surrogate for unresolved turbulent momentum transport and energy dissipation, which can improve reduced-order modeling in solar convection and atmosphere simulations.
method: Trained a 3D convolutional neural network on 3D velocity fields to predict Reynolds stress tensor components.
Included scalar plasma density alongside vector velocity components to improve spatially aware turbulence prediction.
Compared against an MLP and physics-based Gradient/Smagorinsky models, with log-transformed targets to reduce skewness effects.
evidence_signal: The final 3DCNN improved average reconstruction by about 31% on diagonal stress components and about 8% on off-diagonal components versus baselines.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on quiet-Sun simulation data, so generalization to other solar conditions, resolutions, or numerical setups still needs validation.
paper_title: Developing Machine Learning Models of Subgrid Turbulent Transport for Quiet Sun 3D Radiative Hydrodynamic Simulations
